# F4 · Captain and vice-captain calls

*Extracted verbatim from the PRD, which remains the single source of truth for every criterion below. Edit the PRD, then regenerate — never edit this file.*

Identifiers in this file: `F4-AC-01` – `F4-UP-02`.
Load alongside this file: `ENGINE.criteria.md`.

#### F4 · Captain and vice-captain calls

| Section | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Priority | **Must.** A named weekly decision in 2.1 that always renders, even as a keep reading. |
| Serves | The first core job in Section 2.3 — the captaincy decision. |
| Happy path | The Captain tab carries one call: a ranked table of all fifteen squad members, in the engine's own ranking order, whose top two rows are the recommended captain and vice. The manager's current captain and vice are marked with C and V badges on their own rows, which is a different thing from the recommendation. The columns are player, form, projected points and this gameweek's fixture, and a bench player carries the same S / S1 / S2 / S3 badge the Squad stat table uses. He accepts or rejects the call with the same three tiles and the same swipe as every other call; the rows themselves are not tappable. |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **F4-AC-01** | **The armband is one call, and it advises on both the captain and the vice every week by construction** — a table ranking the whole squad always states who should wear each, so the advice cannot go missing in a quiet week. The manager accepts or rejects it with the same three tiles and the same swipe as every other call. **Where both armbands already sit on the recommended pair it is a keep reading:** shown, non-interactive, and outside every tally. On the Overview the armband is stated in one code-written line — "Captain: X. Vice: Y." — and its call row reads as a result rather than a move, with no arrow. |
| **F4-AC-05** | What is captaincy-specific is the reasoning block and the vice premise: eligibility, and the fact that the vice armband only pays if the captain does not play. **Rotation risk is not among them** — rotation left the engine on 2026-09-09 (#74): no input, no multiplier, no gate, and a rotation-risky player simply carries a low projection. **The vice premise survives the removal of its arithmetic, and that is deliberate rather than an oversight.** The armband genuinely does only pay if the captain misses; what changed on 2026-09-10 (#80) is that the *net* stopped pricing it, because no source publishes the probability. This criterion governs the reasoning block — the words on the card — so under *disclose uncertainty, do not price it* it is now the only place the premise is expressed at all. Striking it because the arithmetic dropped it would remove the disclosure and keep neither. |
| **F4-AC-13** | **The call is a ranked table of all fifteen squad members, and the order is the engine's ranking** — projected points, except where the captaincy ceiling tie-break (3.2) displaces it within the noise floor — **so the top two rows are the recommended captain and vice by construction.** Sorting on the figure alone would disagree with the ranking it is meant to show, because the tie-break rules a band rather than a tie: it put the captain mark on row 2 with the table's own evidence arguing against its conclusion. **The visible consequence is stated rather than hidden:** the projected-points column is occasionally out of descending order, by at most the noise floor, and always on a row that says why. Its columns are player, form, projected points and this gameweek's fixture, and a bench player carries the same S / S1 / S2 / S3 badge the Squad stat table uses. **The manager's current captain and vice are marked separately, with C and V badges on their own rows** — what he holds and what is recommended are two different things and are never conflated. **The rows are not tappable:** the table is a reading rather than a picker, and he does not choose his own captain here. |
| **F4-AC-14** | **The pool is the whole squad as it stands, and exactly two things bar a player from the armband:** he fails the availability gate (3.2), or his club has no fixture this gameweek. A barred player is still listed, ranked below every eligible one, and cannot be the recommended captain or vice. **Being on the bench does not bar him, and neither does being named in a transfer or substitution the manager has not accepted** — excluding him would decide that call on his behalf. The accepted cost is that a player being transferred out can top the table (#105). |
| **F4-AC-15** | **The figure on the card is the captain move, and it is labelled `xPTS` rather than "strength."** The captain is what doubles: the week scores 2B + A instead of 2A + B, so the gain is the plain difference, taken once. Where the captain does not move but the vice does, the figure is the vice's. **The two are never summed** — the manager collects one or the other, never both. It is never labelled *strength*, because beside a ranked table that word reads as confidence in the pick, which this figure does not measure — **the conviction chip next to it is what measures confidence.** `xPTS` is what the app calls a projected-points difference on every other surface (the Overview rows, the card figures strip, the squad stat table), and the armband was the only figure carrying a phrase of its own. **There is no cost cell on this call**: no money moves and no transfer is used, and a money column only ever appeared here because the swap framing carried one (#104). |
| **Unhappy Paths** |  |
| **F4-UP-01** | **A squad member has two fixtures this gameweek, or none.** Acceptance: the same blank/double grammar as F1 — the fixture column carries both fixtures or reads BLANK, and the projected-points column sums or zeroes accordingly. A player whose club has no fixture cannot take the armband (F4-AC-14), so the blank case is settled by the ranking rather than on the card. |
| **F4-UP-02** | **The call is rejected.** Acceptance: both armbands stand exactly as the manager holds them and the card carries its rejected state like any other. There is no second armband call left to hold, so an inconsistent pair cannot arise. |
